title: Print-in-Place Hinged Strap-Tail Clamp with Snap Latch
description: A 58 x 89 mm clamshell with a five-knuckle print-in-place hinge, grip ribs and a flexure snap tab. Folds shut over loose webbing tails (backpack straps, tent straps, sling straps) and clicks closed.
use: Open it flat, lay the strap tail across the ribs, fold the lid over until it clicks. Thumb-press the tab to open. Also holds spare cord or a bundle of tent pegs flat against a strap.
material: PETG, 0.2 mm layers, 4 perimeters, print flat (open) with no supports. Hinge clearance 0.4 mm: may need a few flexes to free after printing.

problem_solved: Loose webbing tails flap and catch on branches or rattle against gear; most strap keepers are rubber loops that fray or fall off. This hinged clamp holds tails flat and opens one-handed, and it prints as a single assembled piece.
mechanism: Five-knuckle print-in-place hinge (pin fused to lid knuckles, free-turning in the base knuckles); two staggered grip-rib sets; a cantilever snap tab with a barb that clicks under a ledge window.
tolerances: Hinge: 0.4 mm axial gaps, 0.4 mm pin clearance, 0.5 mm leaf-to-knuckle; snap barb 0.8 mm overlap; closed webbing gap 3.2 mm; ribs 0.8 mm apart when closed.
assembly: 2. After printing flex the hinge a few times to break any layer bonds across the 0.4 mm gaps.
3. Lay webbing across the ribs, fold the lid down until it clicks.
fit_notes: Sized for 25 mm webbing (two layers). No supports; hinge gap bridges over 0.4 mm - ironing/first layer squish may fuse the knuckles on some printers.
